title: The Columbian Exchange: crops, animals and diseases between two worlds
examples: Which foods came from the Americas?
Why did so many Indigenous Americans die after 1492?

nodes.label: The Americas
nodes.ask: Which foods came from the Americas?

explain.say: Imagine Indian food without chilli, Italian food without tomatoes, or Irish history without the potato. All three came from the Americas after 1492. The historian Alfred Crosby named this two-way flow the Columbian Exchange in 1972. Look at the network: four continents swapping plants, animals and germs.

draw.text: The Columbian Exchange: crops, animals and diseases between two worlds

explain.say: Start with the sorting board. From the Americas came maize, potatoes, tomatoes, chilli and cacao. To the Americas came wheat, horses, cattle, sugar cane and, terribly, smallpox. Can you guess which crop helped Europe's population grow fastest?

Answer: the potato. Economists Nathan Nunn and Nancy Qian estimated it explains about a quarter of Old World population growth between 1700 and 1900. Look at the map. Portuguese traders brought chilli to India, and Spanish galleons took sweet potatoes and maize via Manila to Asia. Which foods on your plate today crossed an ocean?

Now the darkest link. Indigenous Americans had no immunity to smallpox, measles and influenza. See the sizes: one 2019 study estimated about 60 million people in 1492 and about 6 million by 1600. Disease worked alongside war, forced labour and famine. Why do historians insist on naming all these causes together?

draw.text: Estimates vary widely; this is Koch and colleagues, 2019.

explain.say: Labour shortages in the Americas also drove the Atlantic slave trade, bringing millions of Africans to sugar plantations. So the exchange shaped what the world eats and who lives where. Thoughtful work today. Challenge: list three dishes from your country and trace one ingredient to its home continent.

nodes.label: The Americas
nodes.ask: Which foods came from the Americas?

faq.a: The transfer of plants, animals, people and diseases between the Americas and the rest of the world after Columbus's voyage in 1492. Alfred Crosby coined the term in 1972.

faq.q: Which foods came from the Americas?
faq.a: Maize, potatoes, sweet potatoes, tomatoes, chilli peppers, cacao, cassava, peanuts, vanilla and many squashes and beans, now staples from Ireland to India, Nigeria and China.
asks: Where did potatoes and tomatoes come from?
What did the Americas give the world?

faq.q: Why did so many Indigenous Americans die after 1492?
faq.a: Diseases such as smallpox, measles and influenza, to which they had no immunity, combined with war, enslavement, forced labour, displacement and famine. Population falls of around 90 percent in many regions are estimated.
asks: What diseases did Europeans bring to the Americas?

faq.q: How did the potato change the world?
faq.a: The potato gave many calories per hectare in cool climates. Nunn and Qian estimate it accounts for about a quarter of the growth in Old World population and urbanisation between 1700 and 1900. Over-reliance also made Ireland's 1840s famine catastrophic.
asks: Why was the potato so important?

faq.q: How was the Columbian Exchange linked to slavery?
faq.a: As Indigenous populations collapsed, European colonists turned to enslaved Africans for labour, especially on sugar plantations, so the exchange and the Atlantic slave trade grew together.
asks: Why did sugar lead to slavery?

facts: Alfred Crosby published The Columbian Exchange in 1972.
Chilli peppers were brought to India by Portuguese traders in the sixteenth century.
Nunn and Qian (2011) estimated the potato explains about a quarter of Old World population growth from 1700 to 1900.

quiz.say: Which of these came FROM the Americas?
quiz.why: Tomatoes were domesticated in the Americas and spread worldwide after 1492.

wrong.1: Wheat came from the Fertile Crescent and went to the Americas.
wrong.2: Sugar cane came from New Guinea and South Asia, taken to the Americas by Europeans.

quiz.say: One estimate gives 60 million people in the Americas in 1492 and 6 million in 1600. What percentage fall is that?
quiz.show: From 60 to 6 million is a fall of…
quiz.why: 60 minus 6 is 54 million lost, and 54 out of 60 is 90 percent.

wrong.1: 10 percent is the share that survived, not the fall.
wrong.2: 54 is the number of millions lost, not a percentage.
